papers.title_en: TrajLong: Co-Designing Agentic and Long-Context Supervision for Mid-Training
papers.authors: Miao Peng, Qintong Zhang, Nuo Chen, Yuhan Li, Guochen Yan, Xinran Gu, Hongqiu Wu, Hai Wang, Lydell Huang, Wentao Zhang, Jia Li
papers.evidence: 将智能体轨迹编译为中期训练长上下文监督
papers.tldr: 长上下文能力对代码、搜索等LLM智能体聚合长交互历史至关重要，但如何将智能体轨迹组织为有效中期监督仍不明确。TrajLong把轨迹编译成带稠密监督的长上下文训练任务，聚焦证据定位、跨证据聚合和时序状态维护。基于Qwen3-14B/30B-A3B中期训练并SFT后，模型在6个长上下文和12个智能体基准上广泛提升，且优于原始与掩码轨迹基线。该工作揭示长上下文与智能体原子能力的任务依赖关联，为下游智能体中期训练数据设计提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: LLM agents for coding, search, and workplace tasks increasingly rely on long-context capabilities to effectively aggregate and reason over extended interaction histories. Recent work has incorporated agent trajectories into mid-training stage, drawing on their naturally long and interaction-rich structure. Yet how to organize the information within these trajectories into effective mid-training supervision remains underexplored. In this work, we investigate the relationship between long-context and agent atomic capabilities and introduce TrajLong, a novel framework that compiles trajectories into long-context training tasks with dense supervision, targeting three representative atomic capabilities: evidence grounding, cross-evidence aggregation, and temporal state maintenance. We mid-train Qwen3-14B-Base and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base with data compiled by TrajLong, followed by supervised fine-tuning. Experiments on 6 long-context and 12 agent benchmarks demonstrate broad performance gains, with controlled ablations showing improvements over raw and masked trajectory baselines. Capability-level analyses further reveal task-dependent associations between long-context and agent atomic capabilities. These findings suggest that the shared capability demands of long-context reasoning and agent execution provide a principled basis for designing mid-training data to develop downstream agent capabilities.

papers.title_en: SynCo: Data Synthesis Co-Training for Self-Evolving LLMs via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Wei Yang, Shawn Li, Yuehan Qin, Yawei Wang, Mingxi Wang, Shixuan Li, Tiankai Yang, Jiate Li, Jesse Thomason, Xuezhe Ma, Yue Zhao
papers.evidence: 面向自演化大模型智能体的智能体数据合成协同训练
papers.tldr: 自进化LLM智能体依赖持续训练经验，但静态数据或单独更新合成模型会造成任务难度与能力错配。SynCo用多智能体强化学习联合优化Synthesizer与Reasoner，由合成任务产生多条rollout并给双方互补奖励。在八个数学推理基准上显著优于多种合成数据方法和受控基线，整体最佳且增益多来自此前未解问题。其贡献是让解题策略与训练分布协同演化。
papers.abstract_en: Self-evolving LLM agents promise to improve autonomously through continual interaction and learning, reducing their dependence on manually curated supervision. Realizing this promise requires not only updating the agent, but also evolving its training experience as its capabilities change. However, most existing pipelines rely on static datasets or separately updated synthesis models, causing previously useful tasks to become trivial while overly difficult tasks remain uninformative. This growing mismatch between agent capability and training experience limits sustained self-improvement. To address this problem, we propose SynCo, an agentic data synthesis co-training framework for self-evolving LLMs based on multi-agent reinforcement learning. SynCo jointly optimizes two independently parameterized agents: a Synthesizer that constructs training tasks from the Reasoner's evolving capability state, and a Reasoner that learns from the resulting experience. Each synthesized task induces multiple Reasoner rollouts whose outcomes provide complementary rewards to both agents. Correctness feedback improves the Reasoner, while task quality, answer reliability, and outcome-grounded teachability guide the Synthesizer. Their updates are fed back into subsequent synthesis rounds, allowing the task-solving policy and its training distribution to evolve together. Extensive experiments across eight mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that SynCo substantially outperforms a broad range of existing synthetic-data methods and controlled baselines, achieving the strongest overall performance while deriving most of its gains from previously unsolved problems.

papers.title_en: Adapting English Quality Classifiers for Multilingual LLM Pretraining Data Selection
papers.authors: Vinko Sabolčec, Bettina Messmer, Yassine Turki, Martin Jaggi
papers.evidence: 将质量分类器多语言适配用于LLM预训练数据选择
papers.tldr: 低资源语言标注数据稀缺，使基于模型的高质量预训练数据过滤难以扩展到百种语言。本文提出将英语质量分类器多语言化的适应方法：在多语言文本上，于Transformer编码器嵌入之上训练小型MLP，并以机器翻译文本的英语分类器得分为标签。1B/3B/8B实验表明，该方法下游LLM基准表现与现有多语言过滤基线相当，且不损害区域文化知识基准。进一步分析显示分类器能跨语言泛化，学习原英语变体的评分标准，即使目标语言未参与训练。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in large language model (LLM) pretraining highlight the role of high-quality training data in improving performance. While model-based filtering has proven effective in selecting high-quality subsets from web-scale corpora, especially for high-resource languages, low-resource languages face challenges due to limited availability of annotated data. This work explores extending quality filtering to over 100 languages by proposing a multilingual adaptation approach that converts an existing English quality classifier into a multilingual variant. Our approach proposes training a small multi-layer perceptron on top of Transformer encoder-only model embeddings, using multilingual text as input and scores obtained from English classifiers applied to machine-translated text as labels. Our 1B, 3B and 8B scale experiments show that our approach maintains the downstream LLM benchmark performance of existing multilingual model-based filtering baselines, without harming regional and cultural knowledge benchmarks. To further evaluate cross-lingual generalization, we compare classifier scores of high-quality synthetic data and web samples, and the correlation of classifier scores with LLM-based ones, revealing that the classifier can learn the scoring criteria of its original English variant, even for languages not included in its training data.

papers.title_en: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study
papers.authors: Ruomeng Ding, Qianli Shen, Zhaoyang Han, Meixin Chen, Daoyuan Chen, Yaliang Li
papers.evidence: 面向大模型训练数据选择、奖励与课程设置的智能体数据工程
papers.tldr: LLM数据工程需反复实验来确定数据选择、奖励与课程如何影响学习，适合AI-for-AI研究。本文提出ADE框架，让智能体依据累积实验反馈提出、修订或组合研究方向，并以闭环分数筛选策略、在留出基准上评估。在数学与代码数据选择、数学奖励设计和数学课程学习四类任务中，所选策略在固定训练下最高带来AIME25 Pass@32绝对提升13.34%，四项留出基准平均提升5.85%。研究还发现闭环分数持续上升但后期收益未必泛化，结合证据分析与累积发现更有效。
papers.abstract_en: LLM data engineering requires iterative experimentation to determine how data selection, rewards, and curricula affect model learning, making it a natural setting for AI-for-AI (AI4AI) research. Can agents use experimental feedback to progressively improve strategies, and do the resulting strategies improve target-model performance on held-out data? We study how agents use experimental feedback to develop data-engineering strategies under fixed training and evaluation protocols. Our Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework lets agents pursue, revise, or combine research directions using cumulative findings. Strategies are selected by in-loop scores and evaluated on held-out benchmarks. Across four tasks-math and code data selection, math reward design, and math curriculum learning-selected strategies achieve absolute gains over generic baselines of up to 13.34% on AIME25 Pass@32 and 5.85% averaged across four held-out benchmarks under fixed training conditions. In-loop scores improve over successive experiments, while held-out trajectories show that later in-loop gains do not always improve generalization. Comparisons of research organization and feedback access favor combining evidence analysis with cumulative findings. Research trajectories show how earlier findings inform strategy revisions and combinations across research directions.

papers.title_en: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
papers.authors: Anni Zou, Cheng Chen, Jiaji Deng, Weikang Zhou, Xinji Mai, Yue Wu, Jianing Lin, Lipeng Xie, Lixiong Qin, Qingyue Zhao, Que Shen, Shuchang Tao, Xuchen Pan, Yaliang Li, Yunpeng Zhai, Yushuo Chen, Zhihai Wang, Zhuo Zhang, Zhaoyang Liu, Bolin Ding, Jingren Zhou
papers.evidence: 合成带状态用户模拟器的协作环境用于后训练
papers.tldr: 协作智能体需跨工具文件处理依赖并适应用户改动，规模化构建一致环境困难。Cowork-Gym用构建-执行-修订循环，结合执行证据与评审反馈验证修复环境，并以有状态用户模拟器通过对话和直接编辑响应智能体。作者合成64.9K个环境、覆盖14类应用，后训练9B/27B/35B-A3B Qwen模型。六项基准平均提升8.7/6.4/4.1分，27B综合第二并在PawBench、ClawEval居首。
papers.abstract_en: Cowork agents navigate dependencies across tools and files while adapting to changing user requirements and edits to shared workspaces. Scaling such environments requires maintaining consistency among task objectives, executable resources, user behavior, and success criteria. We introduce Cowork-Gym, a framework that synthesizes Cowork environments through a build-execute-revise loop that uses execution evidence and review feedback to validate and repair generated environments. To capture realistic Cowork dynamics, a stateful user simulator responds to the agent's actions through dialogue and direct edits to the shared workspace. We synthesize 64.9K environments across 14 application scenarios and use them to post-train 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B Qwen models with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation. Averaged across six agentic benchmarks, these models outperform their corresponding base checkpoints by 8.7, 6.4, and 4.1 points, respectively. Ours-27B ranks second overall among the evaluated models and achieves the highest average scores on PawBench and ClawEval, outperforming models with over 100B total parameters on both benchmarks.

papers.title_en: WorkRover: Scaling Long-Horizon Cowork Agent Training Via Recursive Environment Evolution
papers.authors: Hang He, Linting Wang, Guanming Liu, Bo Mao, Jinxiu Liu, Yiran Suo, Maosen Zhou, Zhiheng Xi, Guanting Dong, Zhou Shao, Rui Zheng, Jie Zhou, Chengcheng Wan, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xipeng Qiu, Xuanjing Huang
papers.evidence: 通过递归环境演化训练长时程协作智能体的框架
papers.tldr: 长时程协作智能体训练依赖可扩展的交互环境，但初始生成环境常需反复测试与修复，且任务缺陷修正还需同步更新工作上下文和验证器。WorkRover 通过 harness 驱动合成，让构建智能体联合生成并校验语义对齐的工作上下文、可执行任务与证据验证器，并引入 FCR 基于回放反馈筛选最小有效修复、VTCA 利用工作区进度检查细化轮次信用。基于 Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 后训练得到的 WorkRover-35B-A3B 在 JobBench、OfficeQA Pro 和 GDPval v2 上均显著优于基线。该工作为可扩展长时程协作智能体训练提供了新框架。
papers.abstract_en: Scaling interactive environments is important for training long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning. These environments often require further testing and refinement after initial generation, and correcting defects in a task may also require updating its work context and verifier. However, existing construction pipelines offer limited support for such iterative refinement while keeping these components aligned. We introduce WorkRover, a framework for training long-horizon cowork agents through recursive environment evolution. Its harness-driven synthesis enables construction agents to jointly build and validate semantically aligned work contexts, executable tasks, and evidence-grounded verifiers, adapting their actions to workspace state and execution feedback rather than following a fixed construction workflow. To support environment evolution, we introduce Factorial Compatibility Replay (FCR), which uses rollout feedback to evaluate combinations of component revisions through dependency-closed replay and selects the smallest validated repair among tested candidates while preserving task requirements and evaluation constraints. To provide finer-grained training signals, we propose Verifier-to-Turn Credit Assignment (VTCA), which augments trajectory-level GRPO advantages with signals from deterministic workspace-progress checks and assigns a bounded share of positive-progress credit to prerequisite turns using recorded tool-output and artifact dependencies. Using WorkRover, we post-train Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to obtain WorkRover-35B-A3B and evaluate it on several cowork-agent benchmarks. Its reported scores exceed those of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B by 26.27 percentage points on JobBench, 29.32 percentage points on OfficeQA Pro, and 413.25 Elo points on GDPval v2. These results suggest that WorkRover offers a promising foundation for scalable training of long-horizon cowork agents.

papers.title_en: C3: Rethinking Process Supervision via Confidence-Guided Credit Correction in Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Ai Jian, Haoran Pan, Eryu Guo, Haojin Yang, Jinghan He, Xiaoyun Zhang, Jiangbo Pei, Peiyu Liu
papers.evidence: 带工具调用的多轮强化学习智能体与信用校正
papers.tldr: 多轮工具调用智能体若仅用结果监督强化学习，成功轨迹中的不良局部行为也会获得正token优势并被策略偏好。为此提出即插即用的置信度引导信用修正方法C3：定位不良行为片段，在优势估计后选择性修正正信用，修正强度由行为策略对该行为的置信度自适应控制，且不改任务奖励与原始信用估计。在多个多轮基准上，C3在基于critic与无critic的强化学习方法下均提升性能。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models are increasingly trained as multi-turn agents that interact with external tools. However, outcome-only reinforcement learning can produce a form of misguided reinforcement: even on successful trajectories, undesirable local behaviors may receive positive token-level advantages and be favored by the policy update. To address this issue, we propose Confidence-Guided Credit Correction (C$^3$), a plug-in method for local credit correction. C$^3$ identifies spans corresponding to undesirable behaviors and selectively corrects positive credit after advantage estimation, with the correction strength adaptively controlled by the behavior policy's confidence in the corresponding behavior, while leaving the task reward and original credit estimation unchanged. Across multiple multi-turn benchmarks, C$^3$ improves performance under both {critic-based and critic-free reinforcement learning methods}. Injecting the same behavioral signals as turn-level or outcome rewards does not consistently improve performance. Our results show that local credit correction provides an effective form of process supervision for outcome-driven RL.

papers.title_en: Tree-Aware Posterior Distillation for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Heming Zou, Qi Wang, Yixiu Mao, Yun Qu, Yuyi Guo, Zeyuan Liu, Chenglin Li, Weijie Liu, Saiyong Yang, Xiangyang Ji
papers.evidence: 长时程智能体多轮强化学习中的信用分配与策略陈旧问题
papers.tldr: 长程智能体强化学习仅用终端奖励，轮级信用分配稀疏且高方差；固定 rollout 上顺序小批量更新还会造成策略陈旧。TreeOPSD 将每轮交互视为树节点，从共享前缀分支续写并递归回传终端奖励，形成隐式轮级信用；再将信用映射为受似然比约束的闭式教师分布，以自蒸馏约束学生策略。实验在多个基准和模型规模上提升智能体能力，Deep Research 中 Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 较 GRPO 平均准确率提高 4.97 分。该框架无需 critic，为长程智能体 RL 提供有界稳定的信用分配与更新。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards has become a scalable post-training paradigm for large language models. However, training agents over long-horizon interactions presents two challenges: using only terminal rewards makes turn-level credit assignment sparse and high-variance, while sequential mini-batch updates on a fixed rollout batch introduce policy staleness as the current policy drifts from the behavior policy. Existing approaches obtain denser credit via learned critics, process reward models, or on-policy distillation, but they rely on a value network, step-level annotations, or a stronger external teacher that increase training complexity. Meanwhile, importance sampling and clipping mitigate policy drift, but they do not specify a finite target that stops sequential updates from overshooting. In this work, we introduce TreeOPSD, a critic-free, tree-aware posterior self-distillation framework for long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning. Treating each interaction turn as a tree node, TreeOPSD branches alternative continuations from shared prefixes and recursively backs up terminal rewards into implicit turn-level credit. It then maps each credit to a closed-form, bounded teacher distribution parameterized by the likelihood ratio relative to the frozen behavior policy. Minimizing the divergence between this teacher and the student policy recovers the policy-gradient direction as the tangent at the behavior policy while bounding updates toward a finite target across sequential mini-batches. Empirically, TreeOPSD improves agentic capabilities across several competitive benchmarks and model scales, especially for long-horizon tasks, e.g., raising the average accuracy of Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 by 4.97 points over GRPO on the Deep Research setting.

papers.title_en: MultiAgent-OPD: End-to-End Training of Hierarchical Multi-Agent Systems with On-Policy Distillation
papers.authors: Yuhan Sun, Jiaxin Zhao, Yongdong Luo, Yibo Hu, Meiguang Jin, Junfeng Ma, Weixun Wang, Weihang Pan, Zhongan Bi
papers.evidence: 结合强化学习的在策略蒸馏用于分层多智能体训练
papers.tldr: 分层多智能体系统中，Leader负责分派任务、子代理执行，但最终答案只能间接反馈子代理表现，联合端到端训练困难。MultiAgent-OPD把同策略蒸馏与强化学习结合，训练共享参数的Leader-Searcher-Answerer团队。训练时冻结的Teacher为Searcher的搜索与摘要token提供局部过程监督，Leader从团队成功学习，Answerer从候选答案正确性学习。在七个数据集上达到38.68% macro avg@4，超过Prompted Critic 4.06个百分点、C-MAS+RL 2.61个百分点，并提升四次尝试内解题数。
papers.abstract_en: In a hierarchical multi-agent system, a Leader assigns tasks and subagents carry them out. Jointly training the Leader and the subagents is difficult because a final answer gives only indirect feedback to the subagents. An LLM judge can score the performance of the subagents, but these scores depend on the judge's own assessment of the quality of subagents' responses. We present MultiAgent-OPD, which combines on-policy distillation with reinforcement learning to jointly train a shared-parameter Leader-Searcher-Answerer team end to end. We first train a Teacher in a Searcher-Answerer workflow using answer correctness. During team training, the frozen Teacher scores student-generated search and summary tokens to provide local process supervision for the Searchers, while the Leader learns from team success and the Answerer from candidate correctness. Across seven datasets, the trained system reaches 38.68% macro avg@4, exceeding Prompted Critic by 4.06 percentage points and C-MAS + RL, the trained cascaded multiagent system, by 2.61 percentage points. The team also solves more questions within four attempts.

papers.title_en: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
papers.authors: Zhongwei Xie, Yiming Du, Jiaxin Bai, Baixuan Xu, Chunyang Li, Xiyu Ren, Wei Fan, Tianshi Zheng, Weizhi Du, Jingqiao Yu, Xingsu Li, Zhaowei Wang, Yangqiu Song
papers.evidence: 为长时程协作智能体合成可执行训练环境与精选数据
papers.tldr: 面向需协调工具、跨轮沟通并遵守流程约束的长期协作智能体，训练经验构建依赖一致的请求、服务记录、工具接口与评分检查。CoworkEnv以能力引导方式合成可执行训练环境，用工作流要求约束任务生成，并通过程序化验证与反馈修复校准规格和评分。教师执行产生SFT示范，学生交互提供RL rollout与奖励，用于训练紧凑PocketWorker。Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct经SFT在Claw-Eval均分由46.6升至64.1，多轮任务提升31.9分，显示环境可支撑策略优化。
papers.abstract_en: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

papers.title_en: Beyond the Teacher: Understanding and Preserving Distillation Overshoot in Agentic On-Policy Distillation
papers.authors: Jike Zhong, Ming Li, Yuxiang Lai, Xi Xiao, Sheng Zhang, Ritwick Chaudhry, Tianle Chen, Jingyu Xie, Zheda Mai, Shao-Yuan Lo, Konstantinos Psounis, Yuanyuan Lei
papers.evidence: 分析基于学生自生成轨迹的多轮智能体在线蒸馏
papers.tldr: 在多轮智能体在线策略蒸馏中，学生模型可能在训练中期反超教师，但继续蒸馏后会回退，作者称之为“蒸馏过冲”。机制分析表明，蒸馏同时修复弱决策与侵蚀教师不认可的成功决策，早期修复占优、后期侵蚀反超。为此提出SPOD，在成功学生决策上屏蔽冲突教师监督并加入软概率下限，同时保留其他位置的教师指导。实验在两类模型族和三个基准上稳定优于普通OPD，最终成功率最高提升15.2个百分点，并可超过教师20.0个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains agents on their own trajectories using supervision from a stronger teacher. We uncover a counterintuitive phenomenon in multi-turn agentic tasks: a smaller, initially weaker student can substantially outperform its teacher during training, only to regress as distillation continues. We term this phenomenon distillation overshoot. Through decision- and task-level analyses, we trace overshoot to two competing effects of OPD: repairing weak student decisions and eroding successful student choices that the teacher disfavors. Early in training, repair outpaces erosion, allowing the student to combine the teacher's corrections with its own strengths and surpass the teacher. As training continues, erosion overtakes repair, causing these gains to vanish. Motivated by this finding, we propose Success-Preserving On-Policy Distillation (SPOD), which selectively masks conflicting teacher supervision on successful student choices and introduces a soft probability floor to counteract their erosion, while retaining teacher guidance elsewhere. SPOD requires only binary episode success and model probabilities already available during OPD. Across two model families and three agentic benchmarks, SPOD consistently outperforms ordinary OPD and evaluated variants, improving final success by up to 15.2 percentage points and surpassing the teacher by up to 20.0 points. Moreover, SPOD's final checkpoints outperform even ordinary OPD's best intermediate checkpoints in all six settings, demonstrating that beyond-teacher gains can be not only preserved but further extended. Code: https://github.com/Jike338/SPOD

papers.title_en: ToolOPD: Credit-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Tool-Use Agents
papers.authors: Chu Zhao, Lei Tang, Yanming Wang, Jianzhe Zhao, Guibing Guo, Zhengzong Chen, Yuanyuan Zhao, Fei Huang
papers.evidence: 在学生自生成工具使用轨迹上做信用感知在线蒸馏
papers.tldr: 长时工具使用中，on-policy蒸馏默认轨迹信用均匀分配，难以识别少数关键动作；最终结果反转还会改变多轮信用，导致监督失准和推理精度下降。ToolOPD将完整轨迹及结果总结为可复用hindsight skill，测量该skill对教师动作token概率的影响以生成结果感知信用，并用该信用重加权动作级蒸馏损失，与强化学习联合优化。多个长时工具交互基准上，ToolOPD显著优于现有强化学习和自蒸馏基线，表明关键动作级监督能提升工具使用智能体表现。
papers.abstract_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) enhances the capabilities of small language agents by providing dense, token-level supervision from a teacher model on student-generated trajectories. However, standard OPD implicitly assumes that credit is uniformly distributed across long-horizon trajectories, assigning the same strength of teacher supervision to different actions. Through credit-distribution analysis and outcome-reversal counterfactual experiments, we find that trajectory credit is concentrated on a small number of critical actions. Moreover, even when the trajectory is held fixed, reversing only the final outcome substantially changes the credit assigned to multiple interaction turns. These findings show that the uniform-credit assumption fails to identify critical decisions and ultimately degrades the model's reasoning accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose ToolOPD, an outcome-aware on-policy distillation framework designed for long-horizon tool use. ToolOPD first summarizes each completed trajectory and its outcome into a reusable hindsight skill. It then measures how this skill changes the teacher's probability of each student action token and converts the change into outcome-aware credit. The resulting credit preserves supervision that supports successful decisions or discourages failed ones, while suppressing irrelevant and conflicting signals. ToolOPD uses these credits to reweight the action-level distillation loss and jointly optimizes it with reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across multiple long-horizon tool interaction benchmarks demonstrate that ToolOPD significantly outperforms existing reinforcement learning and self-distillation baselines.

papers.title_en: Productive State-Space Exploration for Multi-turn RL in LLM Agents
papers.authors: Mohammed Haroon Dupty, Yong Liang Goh, Song Guo, Wee Sun Lee
papers.evidence: LLM智能体多轮强化学习中的生产性状态空间探索
papers.tldr: 多轮长程环境中，LLM智能体常因无效动作与重复循环而陷入高置信却低产出的行为，导致状态表征与环境动态不匹配。为此，作者提出条件状态空间探索框架，用内在奖励惩罚观测重复以鼓励覆盖状态空间，并平衡任务完成与信息寻求。实验显示该方法显著改善多轮策略学习，减少无效动作和重复循环。该工作为LLM智能体的高效探索提供了可操作的奖励设计思路。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement Learning (RL) for Large Language Model (LLM) agents in multi-turn, long-horizon environments remains challenging due to inefficient action selection and repetitive behavioral patterns. In particular, agents often become trapped in high-confidence yet unproductive behaviors, repeatedly executing invalid actions or entering action loops that hinder task completion. We observe that these frequently violate environment preconditions, revealing a mismatch between the agent's representation of the internal state and the dynamics of the underlying environment. In addition, repetitive high-confidence actions lead to cyclical behaviors that provide little to no progress towards the goal. We argue that addressing these challenges requires more productive task-aligned exploration to improve the agent's understanding of environment dynamics. Motivated by intrinsic curiosity-driven exploration, we propose a conditional state-space exploration framework that balances task completion with intrinsic information-seeking behavior. Specifically, we introduce an intrinsic reward that penalizes actions whose observation duplicates prior state memory. This provides the benefit of reducing redundant behaviors and encouraging state-space coverage without relying on a general information-theoretic measure. Strong experimental results demonstrate that our approach substantially improves policy learning in multi-turn environments, mitigating invalid actions and repetitive loops.

papers.title_en: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
papers.authors: Hengqi Liu, Ziyuan Liu, Yang Qin, Wanting Zhou, Zichuan Wang, Jiachen Liang, Xu Chu, Shaowei Chen, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan
papers.evidence: 面向协作智能体的可验证任务合成与长程后训练
papers.tldr: 金融分析要求智能体跨文档整合证据并完成多步数值推理，但专家出题成本高、直接合成任务答案不可靠。Navalia 以企业财报为数据源，语义选取证据并构建可执行计算链，生成带证据溯源与步骤依赖的任务，再用独立审查和程序化检查验证。验证任务用于轨迹收集、冷启动SFT与强化学习，提升长程执行。基于 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 的模型在五个基准上均稳定优于基座，显示方法可泛化至更广泛办公协作场景。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from conversational assistants into Cowork Agents capable of autonomous planning, tool use, and complex task execution. Financial analysis requires these agents to integrate cross-document evidence and perform multistep numerical reasoning, but expert task authoring is costly, while direct LLM synthesis struggles to produce challenging tasks with reliable answers. We introduce Navalia, a framework for Cowork Agents that combines verifiable task synthesis with long-horizon post-training. Using corporate financial reports as its data source, Navalia semantically selects supporting evidence from complete fact sets and constructs executable computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable evidence and actual data dependencies between steps. We further use independent LLM review and programmatic checks to verify evidence consistency and answer correctness. The verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, cold-start supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL) to improve long-horizon task execution. Navalia, initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, achieves consistent gains over the base model across all five benchmarks: OfficeQA Pro, FinSearchComp, Finance Agent Benchmark, APEX-Agents-AA, and Workspace-Bench-Lite. These results demonstrate that Navalia improves evidence integration, tool use, and long-horizon task execution capabilities and generalizes to broader Cowork settings, including general office tasks.

papers.title_en: From Imitation to Reward Discovery: On-Policy Warmup for Agentic RL
papers.authors: Yitong Qiao, Tiantian He, Lei Liu, Yue Shen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Zhixuan Chu
papers.evidence: 在智能体强化学习前用学生交互轨迹做在线蒸馏预热
papers.tldr: 针对RLVR稀疏结果奖励导致早期训练信号不足，论文发现以on-policy蒸馏初始化的RLVR能更早达到高性能并取得更高平均与最终表现。为此提出On-Policy Warmup，让学生先在自身交互轨迹上接受教师监督，覆盖不完美动作与恢复情形，再转入RLVR。理论将on-policy reverse-KL蒸馏联系到轨迹级分布匹配，给出初始验证成功下界与奖励发现复杂度界。结果表明该预热可有效加速智能体RLVR，并揭示初始奖励发现是关键机制。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with a verifiable reward (RLVR) offers a scalable approach to training language-model agents, yet sparse outcome rewards can leave early training with little signal for policy improvement. We identify an On-Policy Acceleration Phenomenon: in our main comparisons, RLVR initialized with on-policy distillation reaches high performance earlier in training and achieves both higher average performance during subsequent RLVR and higher final performance than the alternative baselines. Motivated by this observation, we study On-Policy Warmup (OPW), a teacher-guided stage in which the student trains with teacher supervision on its own interaction trajectories before transitioning to RLVR. Unlike imitation on fixed teacher-generated trajectories, OPW targets states induced by the student's own decisions, including imperfect actions and recovery situations. We provide a theoretical explanation by connecting on-policy reverse-KL distillation to trajectory-level distribution matching. Under a competent teacher and sufficiently small population distillation loss, this connection yields a lower bound on initial verifier success and a corresponding bound on reward-discovery complexity. For group-relative RLVR, we further characterize when increased success probability produces more reward-informative groups. Together, our findings support on-policy distillation as an effective warmup for agentic RLVR and identify initial reward discovery as a mechanism that can contribute to the observed acceleration.

papers.title_en: T2SPO: Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Bo-Wen Zhang, Junwei He, Maoqi Liu, Feiran Li, Song-Lin Lv, Wentao Ma, Rongyi Lin, Shuhan Zhong, Lan-Zhe Guo
papers.evidence: 利用交互轨迹的步级策略优化用于智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: LLM智能体在交互任务中常只收到最终结果奖励，难以判断哪些中间决策真正推动任务。T2SPO从成功轨迹中提取“剩余距离”目标并配对中间状态表示，用预训练TabPFN回归器在新轨迹每个状态上估计剩余距离。相邻状态估计值的变化为智能体步骤提供辅助信用信号，并与任务级奖励共同训练。在ALFWorld与WebShop上，1.5B和7B模型的任务成功率稳定优于GRPO。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning enables large language model (LLM) agents to learn multi-step behaviors through interaction with their environments. However, rewards in many interactive tasks reflect only the final outcome, providing limited guidance on which intermediate decisions advance the task. Successful training trajectories contain intermediate states that can provide supervision for subsequent interactions. We introduce Trajectory-to-Step Policy Optimization (T2SPO), a method that uses past interaction trajectories to provide step-level feedback for policy learning. T2SPO derives remaining-distance targets from successful trajectories and pairs them with representations of the states visited along the way. Conditioned on these examples, a pretrained TabPFN regressor estimates the remaining distance to success at each state of a new rollout. Changes in this distance estimate across consecutive states yield auxiliary credit for agent steps alongside task-level supervision. As training proceeds, newly completed trajectories refresh the estimator's context, incorporating new experience without updating its parameters. Experiments with 1.5B and 7B language models on ALFWorld and WebShop show that T2SPO consistently improves overall task success over GRPO.

papers.title_en: RewardWeaver: Long-Horizon Interactive Learning for Language Agents via Self-Evolving Reward Adaptation
papers.authors: Hengbo Xiao, Boyao Zhang, Purui Liu, Yuxuan Zheng, Haoran Yin, Haibo Liu, Fan Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向长程多轮语言智能体强化学习的自演化奖励适配
papers.tldr: 长程交互语言智能体常受稀疏终端奖励与信用分配困难制约，过程奖励虽更密集，但关键能力会随策略演化而变化。RewardWeaver构建语义固定的已验证能力空间，将策略优化、任务评估、失败归因与奖励适配闭环联动，动态选择下一阶段过程奖励。在SOTOPIA、Amazon HistoryPrice和新销售基准上取得SOTA，消融验证动态奖励分配、失败归因与稳定语义的重要性。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has driven substantial progress in domains where task outcomes can be reliably evaluated, but long-horizon interaction remains challenging due to sparse terminal feedback and difficult credit assignment. Process rewards provide denser supervision, yet the capabilities most relevant for training can change as the policy evolves: a behavior that is easy to evaluate or frequently deficient need not be the bottleneck currently limiting task success. We introduce RewardWeaver, a self-evolving reward adaptation framework for language agents in long-horizon interaction. RewardWeaver maintains a validated capability space in which the semantics of admitted Rubrics remain fixed, and closes the loop between policy optimization, task evaluation, failure attribution, and reward adaptation. After each training stage, it performs outcome-grounded backward attribution on low-outcome trajectories, aggregates recurrent and policy-controlled capability bottlenecks, and dynamically selects the corresponding process rewards for the next stage. Recurrent failures not covered by the existing capability space trigger a separate, controlled expansion procedure. We evaluate REWARDWEAVER on SOTOPIA, Amazon?HistoryPrice, and a newly constructed Sales Benchmark. Across social interaction, bilateral bargaining, and domain-specific sales, REWARDWEAVER establishes new state-of-the-art (SOTA) results. Ablations further demonstrate the importance of dynamic reward allocation, failure-grounded attribution, and stable semantics for admitted capabilities.

papers.title_en: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
papers.authors: Chenxu Zhang, Yaorui Shi, Wenlong Zhang, Jianchao Tan, Zihan Wang, Yiming Cheng
papers.evidence: 通过组策略优化为长程智能体轨迹做信用分配
papers.tldr: 长程LLM智能体训练依赖稀疏终局反馈，组内兄弟轨迹的信用分配需结合上下文与双向证据。MCGPO从已采集轨迹构建加权动作偏好，用动作前状态摘要和任务规则标注的评分进度定义匹配上下文，并以固定折分和证据权重辅助GraphGPO学习。六类环境-骨干设置下，该方法稳定提升平均成功率，WebShop在Qwen3上增益达3.96和5.16个百分点。它复用轨迹、保持无评论家训练，为组策略优化提供可验证的上下文匹配机制。
papers.abstract_en: Training long-horizon language model agents requires assigning credit to intermediate decisions from sparse terminal feedback. Within a finite group of sibling rollouts, useful action comparisons depend on their context, evidence for both alternatives, and how that evidence enters learning. We propose Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization (MCGPO), a procedure for constructing weighted action preferences from already collected trajectories. MCGPO defines comparison contexts with pre-action state summaries and observed rubric progress, annotated by task rules. Two-action support selects among ordered exact and coarse matching rules. Fixed folds separate candidate decisions from the terminal outcomes used to orient their preferences, and support-dependent evidence weights scale an auxiliary pairwise objective alongside shared GraphGPO task learning. MCGPO reuses rollout data and each response's original history, preserving critic-free training. Across six environment-backbone settings with three training seeds each, MCGPO improves mean success over matched GraphGPO: by 0.47-1.46 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B, and by 3.96 and 5.16 points on WebShop with Qwen3-4B and 8B. The ALFWorld gains build on baseline success above 92%, where remaining headroom is limited. Integrated success improves in three of four Qwen2.5 settings. Three-seed factorial controls support opposite-fold evidence and evidence weighting; joint state-rubric matching achieves the highest mean in all four representation-control settings.

papers.title_en: PhantomEnvironments: Training LLM Agents in Fictional Worlds
papers.authors: Anmol Kabra, Swathi Saravana Selvam, Albert Gong, Chao Wan, Christian Belardi, Dongyoung Go, Katie Z. Luo, Kilian Q. Weinberger
papers.evidence: 用于训练LLM搜索智能体的多轮强化学习环境
papers.tldr: LLM智能体强化学习受限于环境需可验证奖励、长程交互且低成本。PhantomEnvironments用纯规则生成虚构世界多跳检索环境，无需LLM、边际成本为零。智能体虽未接触真实事实，却能迁移到真实多跳搜索基准，部分新基准超过真实数据训练。消融显示跳数比约束/比较更驱动迁移，规则生成环境是免费且可泛化的训练资源。
papers.abstract_en: Training LLM agents with reinforcement learning (RL) is bottlenecked by environments, which must provide verifiable rewards, support long-horizon interaction, and scale cheaply. Existing approaches rely on costly human-curated data or on LLM-generated environments that risk hallucinations and benchmark contamination. We show that LLMs can instead be trained into capable search agents using synthetic environments generated entirely by rules, whose generation requires no LLM and has zero marginal cost. We build PhantomEnvironments, multi-turn RL environments from fictional worlds, where agents must search a corpus of templated articles to answer multi-hop questions. Despite sharing no facts with the real world, these strikingly simple environments yield agents that transfer to real-world multi-hop search benchmarks, often outperforming real-world training data on newer benchmarks. Trained agents generalize to unseen fictional universes, and Qwen models learn to scale their search budget roughly linearly with question difficulty, suggesting emergent search scaling from environment interaction alone. Ablating environment complexity reveals that hop count drives transfer more than constraints or comparisons: even the simplest rule-generated environments are a surprisingly effective, free resource for training generalizable LLM agents.

papers.title_en: VenusRL: A Fully Disaggregated Agentic RL System with Priority Scheduling and Scalable Interaction
papers.authors: Mingjun Zhang, Yucheng Li, Menghao Zhang, Shuyong Zhu, Ping Zhang, Xiaohe Hu, Jun Chen, Zhixin Wang, Xutong Wang, He Liu, Yanmin Jia, Shengrong Zhu, Peng Sun, Mingjie Zhang, Liming Liu, Jinlong Hou, Yuan Cheng, Yujun Zhang
papers.evidence: 支撑LLM智能体与外部工具环境多轮交互的智能体强化学习训练系统
papers.tldr: Agentic RL 的多轮交互受最慢轨迹拖累，且工具沙箱按内存上限静态超配，造成训练吞吐与环境资源双重浪费。VenusRL 采用全解耦架构，以长度预测优先级调度跨批次准入、KV Cache 驻留与请求编排，并用内存感知准入和模板键控页共享池提升沙箱密度。在代表性负载上实现最高 4.24 倍端到端加速，环境成本降低最多 89%。
papers.abstract_en: Agentic Reinforcement Learning (RL) trains LLM agents through multi-turn interactions with external tool environments. Its multi-turn nature exposes two system-level bottlenecks unaddressed by existing agentic RL frameworks. First, end-to-end training throughput is constrained by the slowest trajectories to complete, yet optimizing per-GPU utilization alone scatters rollout progress across many groups, delaying the completion of enough groups to unblock the next training step. Second, tool sandboxes are statically over-provisioned by their declared memory ceilings, leaving most physical memory stranded while replicating near-identical state across sandboxes launched from the same prompt. We present VenusRL, a fully disaggregated agentic RL system that addresses both bottlenecks. VenusRL's priority-aware action scheduler uses length-prediction heuristics to identify sample groups whose completion is most likely to unblock the next training step, and pushes them ahead of others across batch admission, KV Cache residency, and cross-worker request orchestration. VenusRL's environment resource manager combines a memory-aware admission threshold with a template-keyed page-sharing pool, packing more sandboxes per node while preserving strict memory isolation via write-protected page table entry aliasing and copy-on-write. Across representative agentic RL workloads, VenusRL achieves up to 4.24x end-to-end training speedup over state-of-the-art baselines and reduces environment cost by up to 89%.

papers.title_en: ThunderSyncRL: Lossless Acceleration of Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Seil Kang, Hangoo Kang, Tarun Suresh, Youngeun Kim, Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar, Seong Jae Hwang, Azalia Mirhoseini
papers.evidence: 面向智能体强化学习的无损加速，支持同策略蒸馏且无策略陈旧
papers.tldr: 智能体强化学习依赖长且异构的交互轨迹，同步训练常因等待采样与验证而闲置学习引擎，异步训练虽能重叠流水线却带来策略陈旧。ThunderSyncRL 在所需输入固定后立即流式计算梯度：GRPO 按单条轨迹奖励到达即计算得分梯度，OPD 在沙箱工具调用期间计算已完成回合的教师评分梯度。方法证明其与批同步更新等价且不改变目标，在两个智能体基准上以最高 1.9 倍速度达到同等性能，固定预算下比异步训练高至多 2.47 个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Language models are moving beyond generating answers to pursuing long-horizon goals in interactive environments. Post-training these agents requires long, heterogeneous trajectories, and synchronous systems leave learner engines idle until rollout and verification finish. To squeeze out these pipeline bubbles, asynchronous training overlaps rollout and learning across updates, but comes at the cost of policy staleness. We introduce ThunderSyncRL, which starts gradient computation as soon as all required inputs are fixed, without policy staleness. For group relative policy optimization (GRPO), ThunderSyncRL computes each trajectory's score gradient as soon as the reward for that trajectory arrives, without waiting for the group. For on-policy distillation (OPD), it computes gradients for each completed agentic turn's teacher-scored actions while tool calls run in the sandbox. We prove that gradient streaming produces the same GRPO and OPD updates as batch-synchronous training, without changing either objective. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal Bench 4.0, we train models to the same performance up to $1.9 \times$ faster than synchronous training. With zero policy staleness, ThunderSyncRL also outperforms asynchronous training at a fixed budget by up to $2.47$ percentage points.

papers.title_en: Structuring MoE Expert Selection for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Bolian Li, Ting-Yao Hu, Cheng-Yu Hsieh, Sanjoy Chowdhury, Oncel Tuzel, Raviteja Vemulapalli
papers.evidence: 面向多轮轨迹的智能体强化学习后训练与专家选择
papers.tldr: 长时程LLM智能体常用稀疏MoE，但智能体行为与专家路由的协同设计不足。本文发现现成MoE的专家选择会按READ、UPDATE等操作形成与轨迹对齐的结构，而标准RL训练未加控制，会破坏该结构并限制性能。为此提出分层路由控制：轮级专家选择对齐智能体操作，词元级选择正则化以保持局部一致性，并用熵门控稳定后训练。多个基准上成功率提升超过10点，表明轨迹结构可有效指导MoE容量优化。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon LLM agents are frequently implemented using sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models, yet the co-design of agentic behavior and MoE structures remains underexplored. In this work, we comprehensively study the connections between agentic post-training and MoE expert selection. In off-the-shelf MoE models, we observe expert selection exhibits a specialized structure that naturally aligns with agentic trajectories. Specifically, expert routing overlaps more between turns where the agent performs semantically similar operations (e.g., READ, UPDATE) than between turns with differing operations. However, standard RL algorithms ignore this specialization, allowing the MoE routing to go uncontrolled during training, which empirically limit task performance and inference efficiency. To address this, we introduce a hierarchical routing control framework for agentic tasks. We explicitly encourage turn-level expert selections to align with agentic operations while regularizing token-level expert selections to maintain local consistency. To resolve stability issues that arise during post-training with the proposed methods, we further introduce an entropy-gated control mechanism. Overall, our routing control framework achieves over 10-point improvements in success rate on all evaluated benchmarks. These results demonstrate that agentic trajectory structure provides an effective signal for optimizing MoE capacity during RL post-training.

papers.title_en: Worse Together: How Performance Breaks Down in Multi-User Multi-Agent Teams
papers.authors: Sahan Paliskara, Nattaput Namchittai, Andrew Lampinen
papers.evidence: 多用户多智能体共享资源下的协作失败
papers.tldr: 用户日益将任务委托给AI智能体，而不同用户的智能体常在代码库、日历、预算等共享资源上相遇并发生协调失败。论文在五个前沿模型、四个环境、77个场景中对比“单一协调者服务所有用户”与“每用户一个智能体”的多用户多智能体团队。结果显示团队在全部环境中群体表现都更差，无通信渠道时两个环境完全崩溃，有渠道时协调开销仍造成显著差距。论文归纳了停滞、互相覆盖、编造声明等失败行为，并提出环境特定的缓解措施。
papers.abstract_en: People are increasingly delegating tasks to AI agents, and those agents are increasingly encountering other people's agents over shared resources such as a codebase, a calendar, or a budget. When each agent acts for a different user with different goals, coordination often fails, and the group ends up worse off than if a single agent had acted for everyone. We study this multi-user, multi-agent setting across five frontier models and 77 scenarios in four environments: an API key environment in which agents share a compute budget, a clinic in which they share a calendar, a personal assistant environment in which they share a group order or booking, and a merge queue in which they share a release cutoff. In each scenario, we compare a single agent that serves every user (a coordinator) to a team in which each agent serves one user, with and without a communication channel between the agents. Teams deliver worse group outcomes than the coordinator in every environment: without a channel, they completely collapse in two environments, and even with one, coordination overhead creates substantial gaps. For example, in the personal assistant environment, the coordinator fulfills a targeted user request about twice as often as teams. We identify distinct behaviors associated with this poor group-level performance, including stalling as teams grow, overriding each other's actions, and fabricating claims. We find effective but environment-specific mitigations, such as a team lead, explicit procedural instructions, and a platform check that makes an agent read its peers' messages before committing. We will release the API key, clinic, and personal assistant environments as MAMUBench, comprising 74 scenarios for evaluating multi-user, multi-agent coordination.

papers.title_en: Federated Agent Optimization
papers.authors: Qiang Yang, Zhiqiang Kou, Xueyi Zhang, Dong-Dong Wu, Hanlin Gu, Jing Guo, Yang Liu, Di Jiang, Qian Xu
papers.evidence: 分布式智能体通过受控信息交换实现跨组织协同改进
papers.tldr: LLM智能体在私有环境中积累记忆、工具使用、反馈与本地知识，但受隐私和产权限制难以直接共享。传统联邦学习只聚合模型参数，无法覆盖智能体能力。本文提出联邦智能体优化（FAO），将智能体效用、隐私泄露与通信成本作为多目标，并在策略、记忆、工具、奖励、结构化知识与技能等空间组织优化。进一步刻画私有经验如何被抽象、保护、聚合与适配为可迁移能力，并总结关键挑战与未来方向。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly operate in private environments and accumulate valuable experience from task execution, tool use, feedback, and local knowledge. Yet such experience is distributed across organizations and cannot be directly shared because of privacy and proprietary constraints. Conventional federated learning is insufficient for this setting, as agent capabilities extend beyond model parameters to memory, tools, rewards, skills, and structured knowledge. In this paper, we formulate \textbf{Federated Agent Optimization (FAO)}, which studies how distributed agents can collaboratively improve through controlled information exchange while keeping raw data, complete trajectories, and private knowledge local. We define FAO as a multi-objective problem balancing agent utility, privacy leakage, and communication cost, and organize its optimization space across policy, memory, tool use, reward, and structured knowledge and skills. We further characterize how private experience can be abstracted, protected, aggregated, and adapted into transferable capabilities, providing a unified view of how agents can benefit from one another without direct experience sharing. Finally, we identify the key challenges of FAO and outline several promising directions for future research toward trustworthy federated agent systems.

papers.title_en: Flowing Faster to Coordinate: One-Step Online Multi-Agent Flow Policies
papers.authors: Zhuoran Li, Yunzhan Li, Xun Wang, Yihan Du, Longbo Huang
papers.evidence: 在线多智能体强化学习协调策略
papers.tldr: 多智能体强化学习需兼顾复杂多模态动作建模与在线训练效率，而扩散策略依赖迭代采样，训练与执行开销较高。OMAF 采用 Transformer 流策略实现单步动作生成，并用近似路径得分代理与联合优化耦合 softmax Q 值，从而学习同步协调策略。在 MPE 与 MAMuJoCo 的 10 个标准任务上，OMAF 稳定优于基线，回报最高提升 3.4 倍，样本效率提升 10.5 倍。该工作表明单步流策略能够在不牺牲表达力的前提下降低采样成本，为在线多智能体协调提供高效范式。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) provides a powerful framework for learning coordinated behaviors through interactions with the environment. Developing MARL policies requires balancing expressive modeling of complex and multimodal action distributions with efficient training and execution. Generative policies, particularly diffusionbased policies, can faithfully capture complex and multimodal behaviors, but costly iterative sampling hinders their scalability in online multi-agent settings. We propose an Online MARL framework via one-step Flow model (OMAF) that combines expressive generative policies with efficient one-step action generation. OMAF employs a Transformer-based flow policy to capture complex coordination behaviors, while its approximate path score surrogate provides a principled route to synchronized flow policy optimization. To enable stable and sampleefficient learning, we further develop a joint optimization scheme coupling softmax Q-value estimation with a joint flow policy objective for coordinated policy learning. By eliminating iterative sampling, OMAF dramatically reduces training overhead without sacrificing policy expressiveness. Extensive experiments across 10 standard tasks from MPE and MAMuJoCo show that OMAF consistently achieves superior performance, with up to 3.4x higher returns and 10.5x sample efficiency improvement compared with baseline methods. These results validate the effectiveness of OMAF as an expressive and computationally efficient one-step flow policy paradigm for online MARL.
